## Study 2. Can the gate tell the operators apart? (the gate sees only the input)

One von Mises-Fisher density model per operator (256 stored inputs each, built exactly like an expert's signature), 24,000 held-out inputs.

- Which operator has the highest density at this input: **87.0 %** right (chance 16.7 %); operator x output slot: **74.9 %** right (chance 2.7 %).
- The nearest stored input has the same operator in 81.8 % of the cases.
- BUT an expert that has never seen operator j still ACCEPTS 88.5 % of j's inputs as familiar (conformal p >= 0.02), against 97.7 % of its own operator's inputs. So the per-sample gate can rank the operators, but it cannot call an operator it has never met "new".
- Geometry: changing only the operator moves the input exactly as far as changing one digit (cosine 0.833 in both cases); two random inputs of the same operator have mean cosine 0.332, of different operators 0.250.

Acceptance matrix (rows: the expert's operator, columns: the operator of the input; % accepted):

| expert \ input | add | sub | mul | mod | div | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| add | 98 | 89 | 87 | 89 | 89 | 89 |
| sub | 88 | 97 | 88 | 89 | 89 | 89 |
| mul | 88 | 88 | 97 | 89 | 89 | 88 |
| mod | 89 | 89 | 87 | 98 | 90 | 90 |
| div | 87 | 87 | 85 | 87 | 97 | 88 |
| max | 89 | 90 | 87 | 90 | 90 | 99 |

## Study 5b. Would the growth have paid off? Capacity added in the middle of the stream

The expert (pool recipe, reservoir 20,000) is grown exactly as the pool does on a commit (function-preserving, optimiser rebuilt) after half of the 4,656 batches; the stream goes on. For the shipped 128-wide expert the candidate sizes are those the policy proposes (+64, +384, +896 hidden units, or one more block); for the capacity-starved 16-wide expert the growth goes to 128 or 512 units.

Starting expert: 128 hidden units.

## Study 5d. Why does the policy miss a capacity shortage? Probe length against the gain it measures

A 16-wide expert after 900 batches of the stream; control and widened candidates are trained for the given number of steps on the stored examples (16,000, mini-batches of 64, fresh Adam, as in the policy's probe) and compared on 4,000 held-out stream examples. Gain = relative reduction of the held-out cross-entropy against the control (the policy needs at least +2 %). For scale: widening the same expert to 128 or 512 units half-way through the real stream raises its accuracy from 11 % to 29-32 % (Study 5b).

| probe steps | control cross-entropy | widen+8 gain | widen+48 gain | widen+112 gain | widen+496 gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 480 | 1.192 | +0.5 % | +1.7 % | +2.1 % | +1.2 % |
| 1000 | 1.199 | +1.3 % | +2.0 % | -0.7 % | -8.6 % |
| 2000 | 1.208 | -0.1 % | -4.1 % | -17.5 % | -66.3 % |
| 5000 | 1.220 | -2.1 % | -21.4 % | -82.5 % | -193.2 % |

Candidate accuracy on the held-out examples after the longest probe (5,000 steps) against the control: widen+8: 58.2 % (control 56.9 %); widen+48: 59.2 % (control 56.9 %); widen+112: 59.3 % (control 56.9 %); widen+496: 59.9 % (control 56.9 %).
